source_constraint: Expected outputs are grounded in @suigar/sdk public event parsing utilities, generated BCS helpers, and numeric conversion helpers.

evals.prompt: I receive Suigar transaction events from Sui. How do I decode a BetResultEvent and get game-specific details without manually parsing bytes?
evals.expected_output: Uses parseSuigarEvent(event) for full decoded game events, or parseGameEvent(event), client.suigar.bcs.BetResultEvent.parse(event.bcs), parseGameDetails({ game, gameDetails: decoded.game_details }), and fromMoveFloat for manual staged decoding.
assertions: Parses event.bcs with client.suigar.bcs.BetResultEvent.parse when showing manual staged decoding
Passes the parsed game into parseGameDetails
Mentions fromMoveFloat for generated Move float structs when showing manual staged decoding
Does not hand-decode game_details byte arrays

evals.prompt: My app receives an unknown generated BCS field that might be a Suigar Move Float or i64. How should I safely convert it?
evals.expected_output: Imports isMoveFloat, isMoveI64, fromMoveFloat, and fromMoveI64 from @suigar/sdk/utils; guards the unknown value with the matching predicate before converting it, and distinguishes this from getGameParameters(), which already normalizes Move float fields.
assertions: Guards an unknown value with isMoveFloat before fromMoveFloat
Guards an unknown value with isMoveI64 before fromMoveI64
States that getGameParameters already normalizes Move float fields
Does not copy a local structural type guard
